heroHeadline: Sulyok Defies Resignation Ultimatum; EU Fund Talks Enter Critical Week
heroSubtitle: President Tamás Sulyok publicly rejected PM Péter Magyar's May 31 resignation demand on May 18, citing no constitutional grounds for early departure and setting up a potential impeachment process. PM Magyar sent a letter to EC President von der Leyen on May 13 outlining Hungary's red lines in the €17B frozen-funds negotiations — including retention of windfall taxes — ahead of a Brussels delegation arriving in Budapest for five days of talks. The full Magyar cabinet was sworn in on May 12, with Economy Minister Kapitány announcing a contractual review of the Paks II–Rosatom nuclear project. TV2 and KESMA executives were removed by May 15 as the restructuring of Orbán-era media accelerated.
footerNote: Tracker covers Hungary's political transition from Orbán's 2010 return to power through the 2026 post-election transition. Data reflects publicly available reports from verified sources.
